answer: A Sybil defense works by making durable identity cost real, unrecoverable collateral, so identities stop being free. An agent must post a bond held for the epoch and slashable by any peer who proves misbehavior. To pose as many agents, an attacker must repeat that deposit per identity, and the capital stays at risk, not merely parked. Anyone trying to forge a terrace of rented identities has to fund every seat, and one upheld slash burns it, so duplicates carry negative expected value. A cheap zephyr of aliases stops being cheap once each must be backed by collateral.
